title: improv·artist · gestural (Cy Twombly)
mutation_directive: improv artist: gestural via Cy Twombly

improv_extras.practice: scribble as handwriting; smeared chalk on cream; eros, mythology, illegibility

v1.feedback: The Twombly brief lands well — epicyclic scribble loops on the Lucy surface read as gestural mark-making, the graphite-plus-crimson palette is restrained and period-appropriate, and the ping-pong trail buffer gives genuine chalk-smear persistence. To push it further: the scribble amplitude (rad) could vary more across body regions so the torso stays legible while extremities dissolve into illegibility, matching Twombly's density contrasts; the crimson strokes (7% via step threshold) could cluster in spatial bursts rather than uniformly scattering, evoking his mythology-panel concentrations; and the slow camera orbit is fine but a very subtle vertical drift or zoom-breathe would add the 'eros' restlessness the brief asks for without losing readability.

v2.feedback: The chalk-smear RT persistence and cream/graphite/crimson palette are genuinely Twombly — the idea clearly drove the shader, not the reverse. Ghost figure alpha at 0.06–0.10 risks making Lucy illegible under the scribble layer; bump ghost base alpha to ~0.12–0.15 or darken ghost color so the mythological silhouette reads in 2s without squinting. Crimson cluster radius 2.8 may bleed too wide on Lucy's compact geometry — tighten to ~1.8 so the red bursts feel like Twombly's deliberate cadmium stabs rather than diffuse wash. Consider adding occasional long single-stroke arcs that cross the full figure height — Twombly's gesture isn't only local scribble, it's also sweeping calligraphic marks that give the panel its scale.
